anu-freq: Clock speed for USB Antminer U1/U2 devices. This is a different miner model; it does not set your L3+ chip speed.
api-allow: Controls which IP addresses can use the mining API and which commands they may run. JMSCNC Heater OS keeps privileged access local to the miner; this field is locked in the dashboard.
api-description: A name included in mining API replies. It helps identify this miner to monitoring software and does not affect hashrate.
api-groups: Defines which mining API commands each access group may use. The format uses a group letter followed by command names. Managed by the dashboard connection settings.
api-host: The network address on which the mining API listens. The dashboard needs its local connection, so this setting is locked.
api-listen: Lets the dashboard read hashrate, temperatures and board status. This stays enabled for the dashboard to work.
api-mcast: Lets monitoring programs discover the mining API through multicast messages on your network. This does not improve mining performance.
api-mcast-addr: Multicast group address used by mining API discovery. Relevant only when network discovery is enabled.
api-mcast-code: Code that a discovery request must contain before the miner replies. The vendor help says not to use a dash in this value.
api-mcast-des: Extra text included in a discovery reply to help identify the miner.
api-mcast-port: Network port used for mining API discovery messages. Relevant only when network discovery is enabled.
api-network: Controls whether the mining API accepts connections beyond localhost. The separate allowed-address list restricts access; JMSCNC Heater OS keeps privileged access limited to this miner.
api-port: Port used by the dashboard to reach CGMiner. JMSCNC Heater OS expects port 4028, so this connection setting is locked.
balance: Distributes work to keep the number of shares sent to each pool balanced instead of using a main pool with backups.
benchfile: Reads mining test jobs from a file instead of a pool. This mode produces no paid pool shares.
benchfile-display: Prints each result found when using an offline test work file. Intended for driver development.
benchmark: Runs test jobs instead of normal pool mining. It produces no paid pool shares.
bet-clk: Clock setting for Block Erupter hardware. This is a different miner model and does not tune L3+ boards.
bitmain-auto: Requests the vendor driver's automatic clock tuning for hashrate. Availability and behavior depend on the driver; it is not a guarantee of lower power use.
bitmain-checkall: A check-all flag for the older Bitmain driver. Its exact effect is not documented for this L3+ build; it is not an L3+ board repair function.
bitmain-checkn2diff: An older Bitmain driver's difficulty-check option. Its exact effect on this L3+ build is not documented.
bitmain-core-temp: Selects a vendor chip-temperature mode, not a target temperature in degrees. The published L3 driver treats this as a mode value; keep the established value unless testing that driver.
bitmain-cutoff: Temperature at which a supported Bitmain driver stops work to protect hardware. Changing a limit does not fix a cooling problem; L3+ support depends on the installed driver.
bitmain-dev: Device path or serial port for the older Bitmain driver. Your L3+ uses its own board driver; this is not a board selection control.
bitmain-fan: Fan percentage or percentage range for an older Bitmain driver, such as 20-100. L3+ manual fan control uses its separate fan-control and PWM settings when supported.
bitmain-fan-ctrl: In the published L3 driver, enables the fixed fan percentage set below instead of normal automatic fan adjustment. Manual speed must still provide enough cooling.
bitmain-fan-pwm: Fan control percentage from 0 to 100, used when manual fan speed is enabled. This is a control signal, not a measured RPM; automatic mode adjusts fans itself.
bitmain-freq: Clock speed used by the mining chips. Higher speeds generally increase power and heat and may cause errors. Your current stock setting is 384 MHz; changing speed cannot repair missing chips.
bitmain-homemode: Requests the older Bitmain driver's home mode. Its noise and power behavior are not documented for this L3+ build.
bitmain-hwerror: Requests hardware-error checking in the older Bitmain driver. The L3+ driver already reports its own errors; this flag may not apply.
bitmain-nobeeper: Disables the beeper on supported Bitmain hardware. It does not change fans or thermal protection.
bitmain-notempoverctrl: Vendor flag for continuing work above the thermal limit. JMSCNC Heater OS displays this option for reference and blocks changes through the dashboard.
bitmain-options: Colon-separated baud rate, miner count, chip count, timeout and frequency for the older Bitmain driver. This is not a simple L3+ performance slider.
bitmain-temp: Temperature a supported older Bitmain driver aims to maintain. L3+ uses its own fan-control implementation; support must be confirmed for the installed build.
bitmain-use-vil: Selects a vendor chip communication mode. The published source uses this option for another Bitmain driver; L3+ behavior is not confirmed. Preserve the existing value.
bitmain-voltage: Raw voltage-control value sent to the board's power controller. This is not a value in volts, and the public source does not establish a safe conversion for your 2019 build. Preserve the established value.
bitmine-a1-options: Clock and chip-count parameters for Bitmine A1 hardware. This is a different miner and does not tune L3+ boards.
btc-address: Address used when mining directly through a compatible node rather than a pool. The vendor option is Bitcoin-specific; it is not your LTC/DOGE pool payout setting.
btc-sig: Optional text placed in a locally mined block's coinbase. It does not change the worker name or payout settings at your pool.
bxf-bits: Clock-tuning value for BXF/HXF hardware, not L3+. It uses hardware-specific units rather than MHz.
bxf-debug: Debug level for BXF/HXF hardware. That hardware differs from your L3+; the public help does not explain each level.
bxf-temp-target: Cooling target for BXF/HXF devices, not L3+ hashboards.
bxm-bits: Hardware-specific overclock setting for BXM devices. It does not tune L3+ hashboards.
compact: Hides per-device statistics in CGMiner's terminal screen. The web dashboard is unaffected.
config: Loads settings from another JSON file. Managed outside this form to avoid replacing the dashboard's validated configuration.
cta-load: Load value for CTA mining hardware, not L3+. This is a vendor scale of 0-255, not measured watts.
debug: Writes extra diagnostic information. It can make logs much larger and is usually useful only while investigating a problem.
default-config: File loaded at startup and used for unnamed configuration saves. JMSCNC Heater OS manages the configuration location.
disable-rejecting: Stop using pools that reject shares
Automatically disables a pool that repeatedly rejects mining results. Other configured pools can then take over.
expiry: How long a mining job may remain usable before results from it are considered stale. Pool notifications can invalidate jobs earlier.
failover-only: Use backup pools only when needed
Keeps work on the primary pool while it is available, instead of sending work to backup pools just because the primary is slow.
fix-protocol: Prevents automatic switching to a different mining protocol. Normally leave this unset so the miner can follow pool protocol instructions.
help: Displays CGMiner's command-line help instead of starting mining. This is a command-line utility option.
hotplug: Time between checks for newly connected USB miners. Zero disables checks. Internal L3+ hashboards are not USB hotplug devices.
hro-freq: Clock setting for Hashratio hardware. It does not set your L3+ board frequency.
kernel-path: Folder containing hardware programming files for drivers that use them. This does not replace the Linux kernel or tune L3+ hashing.
load-balance: Shares mining work between pools according to their configured quotas instead of keeping backup pools idle.
log: How often CGMiner writes its regular status summary to the log. A shorter interval creates more log output.
logfile: File path used for CGMiner log output. Changing the path may affect where diagnostics can be found.
logfile-openflag: Vendor file-opening mode for the log, such as a+ for append. This is a technical file mode, not a log detail level.
logwork: File path for detailed work records. Intended for diagnostics and driver development; it may create large files.
logwork-asicnum: Vendor chip-count value used by detailed work logging. This does not change the number of working chips detected on a board.
logwork-diff: Vendor flag related to difficulty information in detailed work logging. Its exact output format depends on the build.
lowmem: Keeps fewer cached share records to conserve RAM. This changes host-side caching, not the ASIC hashing algorithm.
minion-chipreport: Interval for reporting Minion chip hashrate; zero disables reports. This applies to Minion hardware, not L3+.
minion-cores: Driver-specific core configuration for Minion hardware. The public option help does not describe its format; it does not apply to L3+.
minion-extra: Undocumented additional settings for Minion hardware. This does not apply to L3+ hashboards.
minion-freq: Single speed or a comma-separated list for Minion hardware, not L3+.
minion-freqchange: Time used to apply a Minion clock change. This is a different hardware driver.
minion-freqpercent: Percentage of the target clock used when a Minion chip starts. This does not control L3+ startup.
minion-idlecount: Logs Minion chip idle-counter changes. This is a diagnostic setting for different hardware.
minion-ledcount: Number of slow Minion chips that triggers the status LED rule. This does not control L3+ LEDs.
minion-ledlimit: Per-chip speed threshold used by the Minion LED rule. This does not apply to your Scrypt miner.
minion-noautofreq: Disables automatic frequency adjustment on Minion hardware. It does not disable L3+ fan control or thermal protection.
minion-overheat: Requests an immediate chip stop above 100 °C on Minion hardware. This is not the L3+ thermal protection setting.
minion-spidelay: Extra delay after each SPI transaction for Minion hardware. This does not control L3+ board cables.
minion-spireset: Minion reset rule: i followed by an operation count or s followed by seconds. Zero means no periodic reset. This does not reset L3+ boards.
minion-spisleep: How long the Minion driver waits during an SPI reset. This applies to different hardware.
minion-spiusec: Undocumented timing option for the Minion driver. Exact behavior is not established by its public help; it does not apply to L3+.
minion-temp: Single threshold or comma-separated list for Minion chips. This does not set the L3+ cooling target.
monitor: Runs a command to receive mining log messages. Because it can execute commands, the dashboard displays it as read-only.
multi-version: Saved vendor compatibility setting. The public L3+ source does not explain its values or confirm an effect in your installed build. Preserve the existing value.
ndevs: Lists connected USB mining devices instead of starting normal mining. Internal L3+ boards use another driver.
net-delay: Adds brief delays to reduce load on slow routers. It does not set the pool's share difficulty.
nfu-bits: Hardware-specific clock setting for Nanofury USB miners. It does not control L3+ chip speed.
no-pool-disable: Legacy hidden pool-management flag. Its exact behavior is not documented by the public help for this build.
no-submit-stale: Skips submitting results from work already known to be outdated. A pool may accept some stale shares, so its rules determine whether that is useful.
osm-led-mode: Status LED mode for OneStringMiner hardware. It does not control L3+ LEDs.
pass: Password for a compatible direct-node JSON-RPC connection. Normal pool passwords are edited under Pools & workers.
per-device-stats: Enables verbose per-device statistics in CGMiner output. The dashboard already shows board information separately.
pools: Pool servers, worker names and passwords. Edit these using the Pools & workers page.
protocol-dump: Writes detailed pool-protocol traffic for diagnostics. Logs can include sensitive connection data and grow quickly.
ps-load: Power-supply load percentage for CTA hardware, not L3+. It is not a measured wall-power reading.
queue: Maximum number of jobs kept ready for mining. Increasing it uses more memory and does not guarantee higher hashrate.
quiet: Shows status and errors with less routine logging. This does not silence the miner's physical fans.
quota: Quota and pool URL written as quota;URL for quota-based load balancing. Used when splitting work among pools.
real-quiet: Disables CGMiner terminal output, including useful diagnostics. This does not affect fan noise.
retries: Saved or hidden retry setting. Its meaning and support are not established by the public help for this build.
retry-pause: Saved or hidden delay setting for retries. Its units and support are not established by the public help for this build.
rotate: Rotates between configured pools at this interval instead of using a primary pool with backups.
round-robin: Move to the next pool after failure
When the current pool fails, switches to the next configured pool using a round-robin strategy.
scan-serial: Serial port to scan for supported external FPGA or ASIC devices. This is not an L3+ board diagnostic test.
scan-time: Maximum time spent scanning a job before requesting fresh work. Pool updates may replace work sooner.
sched-start: Legacy HH:MM start time inside CGMiner. Use the single Daily mining schedule section for JMSCNC Heater OS's fan-preserving pause/resume behavior; avoid competing schedules.
sched-stop: Legacy HH:MM stop time; without a start time CGMiner may exit. Use JMSCNC Heater OS's Daily mining schedule for a pause that leaves fan control running.
scrypt: Selects Scrypt where supported by this build. LTC/DOGE hashing on L3+ is performed by dedicated Scrypt chips.
sharelog: Appends submitted-share records to a file for diagnostics. It can grow during long mining sessions.
shares: Exits after the specified number of shares. Leaving it unset keeps normal mining running without this limit.
socks-proxy: SOCKS4 proxy server in host:port format, for routing pool traffic through another machine.
suggest-diff: Suggests a share difficulty to the pool. The pool can choose its own value; this does not increase the ASIC's raw speed.
syslog: Send mining logs to the system log
Uses the miner's system logging service for CGMiner messages instead of standard error output.
temp-cutoff: Generic driver temperature limit, as one value or a comma-separated list. L3+ support must be confirmed for the installed driver.
text-only: Uses simple terminal text instead of the interactive terminal screen. The web dashboard appearance is unaffected.
url: Server URL for a direct JSON-RPC mining connection. Normal Stratum pool addresses are edited under Pools & workers.
usb: Selects which USB mining devices CGMiner should use. L3+ internal hashboards are not selected here.
user: Username for a compatible JSON-RPC mining server. Normal pool worker names are edited under Pools & workers.
userpass: Combined username:password for a direct JSON-RPC mining connection. Stored secrets stay hidden in the dashboard.
verbose: Adds more mining details to standard error output as well as the status display.
version: Prints the CGMiner version instead of starting mining. This is a command-line utility option.
version-file: Vendor file used for miner version information. JMSCNC Heater OS manages this path outside the editable form.
widescreen: Uses a wider CGMiner terminal display. This does not change the browser dashboard layout.
worktime: Logs extra timing information for mining jobs to help diagnose delays.
bitmain-autodownscale-after: Legacy setting preserved from your backup. Public Bitmain L3+ source does not document the meaning or units of this threshold, and stock support is unconfirmed. Preserve the existing value.
bitmain-autodownscale-hw: Legacy hardware-error-related tuning field from your backup. Its threshold units and behavior are undocumented for this stock build; changing it may have no effect.
bitmain-autodownscale-min: Legacy minimum tuning field from your backup. The public stock source does not establish whether this is a frequency or another threshold. Units and support are unconfirmed.
bitmain-autodownscale-prec: Legacy tuning field from your backup. Its precision scale and behavior are undocumented for this stock build. Preserve the existing value.
bitmain-autodownscale-profile: Legacy tuning profile from your backup. The profile choices and stock-build support are not documented, so no performance effect is promised.
bitmain-autodownscale-step: Legacy tuning step from your backup. The public stock source does not establish its units or whether the installed miner uses it. Preserve the existing value.
bitmain-autodownscale-timer: Legacy tuning timer from your backup. Its time units and stock-build support are unconfirmed; it is separate from the dashboard's daily Off/On schedule.
bitmain-chip-freq: Saved per-chip tuning field from your backup. Its format and support are not documented for the installed stock miner; it cannot restore missing chips.
bitmain-fan-rpm-off: Saved vendor flag associated with fan RPM checks. Its stock-build behavior is unconfirmed; it is not a fan speed setting. Preserve the existing value and retain fan protection.
bitmain-maxx: Saved vendor field whose exact meaning, units and support are not documented in public L3+ source. This label refers to the field name only; changing it cannot repair a hashboard.
bitmain-minhr: Saved vendor field whose hashrate units and response are not documented for this stock build. It does not set the physical chip speed.
bitmain-trigger-reboot: Saved vendor reboot-related field from your backup. The triggering conditions and stock-build support are unconfirmed. It is separate from the dashboard's Reboot miner button.
bitmain-freq1: Saved per-board frequency field. Independent board tuning and its units are not confirmed in this stock build; the supported general clock setting is Chip clock speed.
bitmain-freq2: Saved per-board frequency field. Independent board tuning and its units are not confirmed in this stock build; the supported general clock setting is Chip clock speed.
bitmain-freq3: Saved per-board frequency field. Independent board tuning and its units are not confirmed in this stock build; it cannot repair that board's missing chips.
bitmain-freq4: Saved per-board frequency field. Independent board tuning and its units are not confirmed in this stock build; the supported general clock setting is Chip clock speed.
bitmain-voltage1: Saved per-board voltage-control field. It is not a value in volts; conversion and independent control are unconfirmed for this stock build. Preserve the existing value.
bitmain-voltage2: Saved per-board voltage-control field. It is not a value in volts; conversion and independent control are unconfirmed for this stock build. Preserve the existing value.
bitmain-voltage3: Saved per-board voltage-control field. Conversion and independent control are unconfirmed; changing voltage cannot establish or repair the missing-chip fault.
bitmain-voltage4: Saved per-board voltage-control field. It is not a value in volts; conversion and independent control are unconfirmed for this stock build. Preserve the existing value.
